A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReCAP research. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched reliably across relocation and model renaming.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic and real-world CAPTCHA evaluations, general GUI benchmark results, reasoning and self-correction ablations, and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds Instruct-model evaluations, frontier-model comparisons, UI-Vision results, and data-scale and capacity analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the written loss from normalization by total token count to separately normalized reasoning and action losses, changing their relative weighting. Section 4.1 also adapts Instruct models using thinking tags. The core generation and self-correction pipeline remains intact; the PDFs do not establish whether the loss revision reflects an implementation change or a documentation correction.

E1.justification: V2 adds UI-Vision element-grounding and layout-grounding evaluation, extending coverage to harder desktop interfaces and functional-region localization. The seven synthetic CAPTCHA types, 26 real-world types, training data sources, and three previous GUI benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 7 add Qwen3-VL-8B/32B-Instruct, GPT-5.4, and Gemini-3-Flash-Preview to CAPTCHA comparisons. Table 3 adds the Instruct baselines and removes its OpenAI CUA column. These changes substantially strengthen and broaden the evaluated comparator set; Oedipus remains unevaluated.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce Instruct configurations, a 4B capacity check, and 50%/100%/150% CAPTCHA-data conditions. UI-Vision uses custom output parsing, disabled thinking, element accuracy, and layout mean IoU. Existing CAPTCHA sample counts and interaction budgets remain stated as before; newly disclosed training settings are not evidence that earlier protocols changed.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a data-scale saturation study, a 4B ScreenSpot-V2 capacity check, and qualitative inspection of OCR, interaction-sequence, and recognition failures. Section 3.2 also newly reports manual trace inspection. The original reasoning/self-correction ablations and Appendix B case studies are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2 continues the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive results: dynamic CAPTCHA success is 78.60%/84.20% for the new Instruct variants, with GPT-5.4 at 56.80% and Gemini at 59.90%. Original Thinking scores, real-world rows, and main ablations remain unchanged. New UI-Vision, real-world, scale, and capacity results broaden the findings; Gemini leads the full real-world comparison on average. V1's under-three-second execution claim is removed.

T1.justification: The Section 3.3 loss formula is mathematically revised: separate division by reasoning/action token counts replaces division by their combined count. With the stated equal coefficients, these objectives are not equivalent; v2's formula supports the intended group balance. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain native CAPTCHA solving, automated reasoning-action data, and self-correction training. V2 narrows the performance message to strong overall synthetic results and mixed real-world transfer, and replaces the conclusion's lower-latency claim with fewer interaction steps. General GUI preservation is also qualified.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands interpretive boundaries: frontier agents remain competitive, real-world transfer does not establish uniform superiority, and interaction steps do not establish full latency performance. Appendix A newly distinguishes answer-conditioned supervision from verified faithful explanations and identifies missing evaluations. Appendix E interprets failures as perception and recovery bottlenecks and discusses data-scale saturation.

D1.justification: Appendices E.1 and E.3 supply previously missing action/executor specifications and training details, including coordinate mapping, parsing, four B200 GPUs, full-parameter SFT, ZeRO-2, precision, sequence length, batching, optimizer, learning rate, and warmup. UI-Vision prompts are also supplied. These materially improve reproducibility documentation; the code/model/data access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including GUI-Actor, GUI-Libra, Reasoning under Vision, STaR, and UI-Vision, and revises descriptions of existing CAPTCHA solvers. It repositions existing CAPTCHA resources as evaluation-oriented rather than primarily insufficiently diverse. The overarching positioning around native GUI-agent learning remains.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted rewrites to the abstract, related work, results discussion, conclusion, and limitations; distinguishes Thinking/Instruct terminology; shortens the running title; and adds acknowledgments and Appendix E. The original section sequence and most pipeline, prompt, and case-study text remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with new model curves and GUI benchmark axes. Table 1 expands substantially, Table 3 gains grouped model columns and UI-Vision rows, and the original real-world comparison becomes part of expanded Table 7. New action-space, training-configuration, and data-scale tables further expand the displays. Figures 2–8 retain their imagery.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important weaknesses through stronger measured baselines, broader GUI evaluation, and substantially fuller reproduction details. It retains earlier results while acknowledging competitive frontier performance and narrowing transfer and latency claims. The corrected loss specification and explicit rationale-faithfulness limitation improve scientific clarity. Missing uncertainty estimates and unresolved implementation history remain, but the overall gains in evidential credibility and reproducibility are substantial.
